title: Keyboard shortcuts that work anywhere
points: Press Alt+Space in any app to open or close the notch.
Press Ctrl+Shift+F to start or pause a Lock In session without reaching for the mouse.
A new Shortcuts page in the Dashboard lists your keys and the apps and sites the notch opens in one click.
Add a launch shortcut by picking any app, and Overlay tells you if another app already uses a key.

title: Lock In settings that stay in sync
points: Choose your session length and break length in the Dashboard with simple buttons.
The notch and the Dashboard now share one session length, so changing it in either place updates both.
Breaks now last as long as you choose instead of a fixed five minutes.
Fixed: saving another Dashboard setting no longer resets the session length you picked in the notch.

title: An exact battery and a notch that's easier to click
points: The battery level and charging state update the moment Windows reports a change.
A cleaner battery icon shows a plug when you're full and plugged in, and turns red at 20% or below.
The open notch's AI card now shows the tool you're actually working in.
Fixed: hovering a button in the closed notch no longer opens it, so What's new, Restart and play can be clicked.

title: Screenshots that save, and a colour that's yours
points: Every screenshot is saved to Pictures › Overlay, named by date and time, and copied to your clipboard.
Full-screen captures use your display's full resolution and hide the notch while the picture is taken.
Area and window captures are saved automatically and appear under Recent in the notch.
Pick an accent colour from named swatches or your own, with a live preview, and it carries across Overlay.

title: Lock In, rebuilt
points: Lock In runs right in the notch, whether or not the Dashboard is open.
Set a session from 5 to 120 minutes or tap a preset, and Overlay remembers your choice.
While you focus, you see the end time and a progress bar; your week shows as simple daily bars.
The closed notch shows a realistic hourglass whose sand pauses when you pause.
The AI tool you're working with sits beside the pause button, so its limit stays in view.

title: Updates that install themselves
points: Updates now download and install quietly in the background, with no installer windows or pop-ups.
When an update is ready, the notch shows a Restart button; afterwards, a What's new button opens the release notes.
Overlay checks for updates shortly after it starts and regularly while it runs.
Installing is a single double-click, and the first launch opens the Dashboard and shows you where the notch is.
Fixed: notifications and the taskbar sometimes showed "Electron" instead of Overlay's own name and icon.

title: A clearer Dashboard and sharper AI tracking
points: Overview, AI usage, To-dos and Notes have clear titles and plain labels.
Your shareable report is a clean card you can download as an image.
Screen time lists each app with its own icon and proper name.
When two AI tools are working at once, both now appear in the notch.
Fixed: an idle Cursor no longer shows as working, and long Claude Code sessions are tracked again.

title: Minimise to a bubble, and updates you can follow
points: Minimise the notch to a small bubble you can drag to any corner; one click brings it back.
The Dashboard's About page shows update progress and a Restart and update button when it's ready.
The notch's update badge fills as an update downloads and glows when it's ready to install.
Overlay launches at startup by default, and a switch in the Dashboard turns it off.
A new branded installer lets you choose the install folder, and uninstalling keeps your history for a reinstall.

title: Every notch tool, rebuilt
points: Water and Habits track your day with a filling glass, progress rings and a seven-day view.
Capture takes full-screen, area or window shots with a timer; Recorder shows a live waveform.
Screen time charts your day hour by hour, alongside new Wallpapers and Trading tools.
Find now searches every drive and ranks exact matches first.
The notch opens when you hover over it and closes when you move away; you can switch this off.
Fixed: long voice recordings now save reliably.

title: Downloads, ports, breaks and Discord calls
points: See your newest downloads in the notch and drag any of them straight into another app.
Ports lists local servers with the app behind each, so you can open or stop them.
Breaks reminds you to rest your eyes, stand up and drink water, each with its own switch.
Follow your Discord voice call with who's talking, plus mute, deafen and leave, after a one-click connect.
A camera preview lets you check yourself before a call and switches off the moment you leave it.

title: One Dashboard, a private account and live AI limits
points: Settings, connections and tracking now live in one Dashboard with a clear sidebar.
A local account with your name, photo and password keeps Overlay locked, and nothing leaves your PC.
Connect Discord, GitHub and LeetCode, with a live status for each.
While you code, the notch shows the AI tool you're using and how close you are to its limit.
Antigravity usage is now counted, and every AI tool shows its real logo.

title: Your AI tools' limits, live in the notch
points: A rebuilt notch with smooth transitions and a dock that shows one tool at a time.
Overlay finds Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Copilot and shows each one's limits and cost.
Hand your current task to the tool with the most headroom in one click.
Now Playing shows a progress bar and synced lyrics, including a live line in the closed notch.
New tools: To-dos, Notes, Clipboard history, Hardware, Weather, World clocks, Calculator, Shelf, Colour picker and Launcher.
Fixed: dropping files onto the notch now works again.

title: One-click sync across Overlay
points: Click the Overlay mark to rescan AI usage, refresh your limits and update every window at once.
AI usage, To-dos and Notes now live in the Dashboard and match the rest of it.
Fixed: AI usage no longer shows zero for today while a scan is still running.
Fixed: switching AI tools automatically no longer writes files into your projects.

title: A redesigned Dashboard and a tray icon
points: The Dashboard gets a navigation rail, a calendar, lap times and colour-coded streaks.
Overlay now lives in the system tray, so it's always one click away.
Fixed: the focus timer sometimes froze or didn't appear in the notch.
Fixed: the Dashboard now loads reliably and retries if something goes wrong.

title: Pomodoro lengths, streaks and levels
points: Choose your Pomodoro length before a focus session.
The timer stays in sync between the notch and the Dashboard.
Focus sessions are fully tracked, with streaks and levels in an expanded Dashboard view.
New lock screen modes and sharper shortcut icons.
Fixed: new shortcuts now appear in the notch instantly.

title: Automatic updates and a battery indicator
points: Overlay can now update itself, so you always have the latest version.
A battery indicator in the notch shows your charge at a glance.
Shortcuts fetch their app's icon automatically.
Settings gains a redesigned About page.
Fixed: the focus heatmap and the Add Shortcut tab are back in the Dashboard.

title: A Dashboard for your focus, and Settings
points: A new Dashboard shows your focus history as a 60-day heatmap and a seven-day chart.
Add quick shortcuts to the apps you use most.
A Settings window lets you choose your music source and tune how the notch looks and behaves.
Your focus sessions are saved on your PC, so your history is kept between launches.

title: The first Overlay
points: A Dynamic Island-style notch at the top of your Windows screen that expands when you need it.
Lock In, a built-in focus timer, runs right in the notch.
Music controls and quick shortcuts sit one click away.
Overlay gets its own app icon and installer.
